label: The Big Bang
description: The universe begins expanding from an extremely hot, dense state. Space, time, matter, and energy as we understand them originate here.

label: Cosmic Microwave Background
description: About 380,000 years after the Big Bang, the universe cools enough for light to travel freely — the afterglow is still observable today as the cosmic microwave background.

label: First Stars Ignite
description: Roughly 100–400 million years after the Big Bang, gravity collapses primordial gas into the first stars, ending the cosmic 'dark ages'.

label: First Galaxies Form
description: Early stars and gas clump together under gravity, forming the first small galaxies — the building blocks of larger galaxies like the Milky Way.

label: Milky Way Begins Forming
description: Our home galaxy begins assembling from mergers of smaller galaxies and gas clouds — a process that continued for billions of years.

label: Solar System Forms
description: A cloud of gas and dust collapses under gravity, forming the Sun and the swirling disk of material that becomes the planets.

label: Earth Forms
description: Earth accretes from colliding planetesimals; shortly after, a Mars-sized body likely collides with early Earth, forming the Moon.

label: Earliest Evidence of Life
description: The oldest disputed chemical and fossil evidence for microbial life on Earth dates to this period — the exact timing remains an active area of research.

label: The Great Oxidation Event
description: Photosynthetic microbes gradually fill Earth's atmosphere with oxygen, transforming the planet's chemistry and enabling complex life to eventually evolve.

label: The Cambrian Explosion
description: A relatively rapid diversification of complex, multicellular animal life appears in the fossil record.

label: Age of Dinosaurs Begins
description: Dinosaurs emerge and go on to dominate terrestrial ecosystems for roughly 165 million years.

label: Dinosaur Extinction
description: An asteroid impact (and associated environmental collapse) ends the age of non-avian dinosaurs, reshaping the course of life on Earth.

label: Homo sapiens Emerges
description: The earliest fossils currently attributed to anatomically modern humans date to roughly this period, in Africa.

label: Written History Begins
description: The earliest writing systems emerge — the beginning of recorded human history, an eyeblink compared to cosmic time.

label: Today
description: You, reading this, roughly 13.8 billion years after the Big Bang.
